description.narrative: SusBDe Holding B.V. has devised the 'Zero Waste-to-Energy' concept, based on proven technology from the Dutch company Machinefabriek Emmen (MF Emmen) for separating and sorting household waste into raw materials for recycling and from the Dutch company Waste Treatement Technologies (WTT) for dry fermentation to convert the organic waste into energy and compost. SusBDe sells the 'Zero Waste-to-Energy' plants and is partly responsible for the turnkey delivery of the installations. The revenue model is based on setting up and running the factories in partnership with local investors.In India, the government wants to significantly reduce the growth of landfills. Local municipalities are trying to find solutions to this. SusBDe has been working in India for some time to market its 'Zero Waste-to-Energy' installation which can process 1,200 tons of unsorted household waste per day. This household waste is separated and sorted. The non-organic flows are completely recycled. The organic part is used to produce biogas and compost based on dry anaerobic fermentation. The biogas is cleaned and then compressed into compressed biogas (CBG), which can be used as a sustainable transport fuel.The concept of SusBDe therefore offers a solution to a multitude of problems that large- and medium-sized Indian cities face: a growing waste mountain, surface and groundwater pollution, shortage of fertilisers and need for biogas and energy. Potential investors want the assumptions of the business model to be validated through further research and practical testing so that they can then make a final investment decision.
